instruction: Forward all emails from the Outlook account to user.backup2026@gmail.com using a Thunderbird message filter.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully created a message filter in Thunderbird to forward all emails from anonym-x2024@outlook.com to anonym-x2024@gmail.com. Opened Message Filters dialog, created new filter named 'Forward to Gmail' with 'Match all messages' condition and 'Forward Message to' action.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate Thunderbird UI, open Message Filters dialog, create new filters, select match conditions (Match all messages), change action types from dropdown, enter email addresses, save filters
metadata.task_rationale: Same forwarding pattern as original but with a different target email address. Tests whether model can generalize the forwarding capability to a different destination without relying on memorized steps.
metadata.explanation: Task requires creating a message filter that forwards all incoming emails to a different address (user.backup2026@gmail.com). Evaluator reads msgFilterRules.dat and checks for a filter with action 'Forward', actionValue 'user.backup2026@gmail.com', and condition ALL.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the msgFilterRules.dat file from the Outlook IMAP account directory, which is the right file for verifying Thunderbird message filters on the Outlook account.
Metric check_thunderbird_filter correctly parses the filter rules file format, extracting name, enabled, action, actionValue, and condition fields for each filter entry.

Expected rules correctly require: enabled='yes', action='Forward', actionValue='user.backup2026@gmail.com', condition=['ALL'] — this fully matches the instruction to forward ALL emails to that address.
The _match_record utility does exact key-value matching against parsed filters, which correctly verifies the filter properties.
The expected.type='rule' means the framework passes the rules dict directly to the metric as the 'rules' parameter — the metric correctly accesses rules.get('expect', []) without unwrapping.
Postconfig closes the Message Filters window before reading the file, which is appropriate cleanup to ensure the filter file is saved to disk.

Minor note: get_vm_file returns Union[Optional[str], List[Optional[str]]] while the metric expects str, but in practice with single-file config (no 'multi' flag), it returns a single str or None, and the metric handles None correctly.

rule_validation_issues.msg: metric check_thunderbird_filter first parameter type (str) may not match getter get_vm_file return type (Union)
